title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 2: - Leaving the usual caveat here that Niners are not yet in pads and won't be for a few more days. And there won't be OL/DL one on ones until then, either. As always, draw your own conclusions. - Coach Kyle Shanahan again watched practice from centerfield alongside GM John Lynch. Shanahan came out just before 11 am and stayed until the end of the practice, which came around 11:45. He's got a sort of cast on his left hand and was again in sunglasses. Once again, a few players made their way over to say hello during the session. - Players not participating because of injury: WR Christian Kirk (calf), DT Gracen Halton (knee bone bruise), OT Vederian Lowe (high ankle sprain), DL Andrew Farmer (back). Of those, Lowe and Halton seem most likely to take awhile to come back from. Disappointing for Halton, who has a path to an early role on passing downs. - DB Nate Hobbs was back and a full participant after not getting any work on Monday. - During the practice, rookie pass rusher Romello Height ended up going in on a cart because of cramps. RB Jordan James was on his way to another strong practice but didn't do much of anything for the second half of the session. Unclear if there was an injury or just giving opportunities to other backs. - Spotted DE Mykel Williams (ACL) doing some work on the side. He appears to be moving well and making progress. Same for DT Alfred Collins and TE George Kittle, both of whom watched practice from the side. - For those monitoring some of the position battles going on in this camp: the first two safeties up today were Malik Mustapha and Ji'Ayir Brown. Mustapha and Marques Sigle are both getting looks at the spot next to Brown. Brown intercepted a pass from QB Brock Purdy today on a throw intended for Jacob Cowing. Nick Martin (SAM LB) and Connor Colby (LG) again got first look at their spots. Would be a nice development for the Niners (and the 2025 draft class) if Colby and Martin can emerge from camp as starters. - The use of 5-man fronts is going to be a discussion that continues to pick up as the year goes on. It's early but the Niners seem to be doing more than just toying with it as a gimmick here and there. Purdy even acknowledged that things look quite a bit different going against Raheem Morris' defense than what the Niners have done previously. - Speaking of Purdy, he had another solid day save for the interception to Brown but the coverage was quite a bit tighter on Monday. Had Purdy at 7-of-11 today not including a missed deep back for WR Mike Evans because a flag was thrown on Renardo Green for what appeared to be illegal contact. Purdy did miss high for rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling when Stribling had created separation and Green had a nice PBU on an in-breaker for Cowing. Purdy's best ball of the day came on a throw to Evans down the middle right after the pick he threw to Brown. - With Lowe out, it was again Austen Pleasants stepping in at LT on the reps when Trent Williams has been getting a breather. Rookie Enrique Cruz Jr. has been with the backups. - Pads will tell a better story but a nice start to camp for rookie RB Kaelon Black. Black may not have that big long speed of a guy like Isaac Guerendo but he has plenty of burst and is decisive when he sees the hole he likes. If James is OK, should be a fun battle for RB2 behind Christian McCaffrey between those two. - DE Nick Bosa again limited to individual work. We'll see when he gets his first reps in team drills. - QB Mac Jones had a strong day, finishing 8-of-12, though to my view only one of those was a clear misfire (he was too far in front of Ricky Pearsall on a crosser). The others included a PBU by Jack Jones against Stribling that could have drawn a flag, a Mike Evans drop and a play in which Pearsall and Jones seemed to get tangled up. - Adrian Martinez went first with the 3s at QB on Monday but Kurtis Rourke had, perhaps, two of the best throws of the day. On the final reps of practice, Rourke threw a perfect deep out to the left to WR Junior Bergen and followed with another one a bit shorter to WR Malik Turner. It wasn't all positive for him, though as CB Eli Apple baited him into a pick-6 earlier in the session. - Purdy has been impressed by the early returns on Stribling. Much will be made of his speed and separation skills, which is fair. But he's a bigger body who is unafraid to go over the middle. With Jauan Jennings gone, adding someone who brings that size and fearlessness (with plus speed, to boot) could help open things up for Purdy and Co. - LB Fred Warner is clearly happy to be back from the injury he suffered last year. He mentioned it on Sunday how much he missed it and it shows. He's been his usual, active self in practice and has even made it a point to let the media know when he makes a play as he has pointed to the sideline and made a motion like he's tweeting about what just happened. - One small thing I've noted in first two days of camp: Niners are doing some things different in practice in terms of how reps are divvied up. They've been going six reps for the 1s, six for the 2s and three for the 3s. That's a bit more in each sequence than they've done in the past. And on Tuesday, they're having a "jog thru" which isn't open to the media. So, it's not a three days on, one day off setup that has been customary. Perhaps it will go to that but suspect maybe there's been some tweaking to the schedule because of the Australia game and perhaps the fewer full practices means ramping up the reps in the longer sessions. - That's all for today. Niners have the jog through tomorrow then back at it on Wednesday. Thanks for reading.
summary:
Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 2:

- Leaving the usual caveat here that Niners are not yet in pads and won't be for a few more days. And there won't be OL/DL one on ones until then, either. As always, draw your own conclusions. 

- Coach Kyle Shanahan again watched practice from centerfield alongside GM John Lynch. Shanahan came out just before 11 am and stayed until the end of the practice, which came around 11:45. He's got a sort of cast on his left hand and was again in sunglasses. Once again, a few players made their way over to say hello during the session. 

- Players not participating because of injury: WR Christian Kirk (calf), DT Gracen Halton (knee bone bruise), OT Vederian Lowe (high ankle sprain), DL Andrew Farmer (back). Of those, Lowe and Halton seem most likely to take awhile to come back from. Disappointing for Halton, who has a path to an early role on passing downs. 

- DB Nate Hobbs was back and a full participant after not getting any work on Monday. 

- During the practice, rookie pass rusher Romello Height ended up going in on a cart because of cramps. RB Jordan James was on his way to another strong practice but didn't do much of anything for the second half of the session. Unclear if there was an injury or just giving opportunities to other backs. 

- Spotted DE Mykel Williams (ACL) doing some work on the side. He appears to be moving well and making progress. Same for DT Alfred Collins and TE George Kittle, both of whom watched practice from the side. 

- For those monitoring some of the position battles going on in this camp: the first two safeties up today were Malik Mustapha and Ji'Ayir Brown. Mustapha and Marques Sigle are both getting looks at the spot next to Brown. Brown intercepted a pass from QB Brock Purdy today on a throw intended for Jacob Cowing. Nick Martin (SAM LB) and Connor Colby (LG) again got first look at their spots. Would be a nice development for the Niners (and the 2025 draft class) if Colby and Martin can emerge from camp as starters.

- The use of 5-man fronts is going to be a discussion that continues to pick up as the year goes on. It's early but the Niners seem to be doing more than just toying with it as a gimmick here and there. Purdy even acknowledged that things look quite a bit different going against Raheem Morris' defense than what the Niners have done previously. 

- Speaking of Purdy, he had another solid day save for the interception to Brown but the coverage was quite a bit tighter on Monday. Had Purdy at 7-of-11 today not including a missed deep back for WR Mike Evans because a flag was thrown on Renardo Green for what appeared to be illegal contact. Purdy did miss high for rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling when Stribling had created separation and Green had a nice PBU on an in-breaker for Cowing. Purdy's best ball of the day came on a throw to Evans down the middle right after the pick he threw to Brown. 

- With Lowe out, it was again Austen Pleasants stepping in at LT on the reps when Trent Williams has been getting a breather. Rookie Enrique Cruz Jr. has been with the backups. 

- Pads will tell a better story but a nice start to camp for rookie RB Kaelon Black. Black may not have that big long speed of a guy like Isaac Guerendo but he has plenty of burst and is decisive when he sees the hole he likes. If James is OK, should be a fun battle for RB2 behind Christian McCaffrey between those two. 

- DE Nick Bosa again limited to individual work. We'll see when he gets his first reps in team drills.

- QB Mac Jones had a strong day, finishing 8-of-12, though to my view only one of those was a clear misfire (he was too far in front of Ricky Pearsall on a crosser). The others included a PBU by Jack Jones against Stribling that could have drawn a flag, a Mike Evans drop and a play in which Pearsall and Jones seemed to get tangled up.  

- Adrian Martinez went first with the 3s at QB on Monday but Kurtis Rourke had, perhaps, two of the best throws of the day. On the final reps of practice, Rourke threw a perfect deep out to the left to WR Junior Bergen and followed with another one a bit shorter to WR Malik Turner. It wasn't all positive for him, though as CB Eli Apple baited him into a pick-6 earlier in the session. 

- Purdy has been impressed by the early returns on Stribling. Much will be made of his speed and separation skills, which is fair. But he's a bigger body who is unafraid to go over the middle. With Jauan Jennings gone, adding someone who brings that size and fearlessness (with plus speed, to boot) could help open things up for Purdy and Co. 

- LB Fred Warner is clearly happy to be back from the injury he suffered last year. He mentioned it on Sunday how much he missed it and it shows. He's been his usual, active self in practice and has even made it a point to let the media know when he makes a play as he has pointed to the sideline and made a motion like he's tweeting about what just happened. 

- One small thing I've noted in first two days of camp: Niners are doing some things different in practice in terms of how reps are divvied up. They've been going six reps for the 1s, six for the 2s and three for the 3s. That's a bit more in each sequence than they've done in the past. And on Tuesday, they're having a "jog thru" which isn't open to the media. So, it's not a three days on, one day off setup that has been customary. Perhaps it will go to that but suspect maybe there's been some tweaking to the schedule because of the Australia game and perhaps the fewer full practices means ramping up the reps in the longer sessions. 

- That's all for today. Niners have the jog through tomorrow then back at it on Wednesday. Thanks for reading.

title: 49ers training camp practice #2 is in the books. Here are some of the highlights: 🏈De'Zhaun Stribling is getting OPEN — catch-and-run house call from Mac Jones with those long 4.36 strides... The rookie also created separation down the seam on a ball Purdy overshot. Stribling caught a nice one from Purdy on an early rollout 🏈New CB Jack Jones has looked spry, but Ricky Pearsall cooked him on a double move — Jones misfired but that was some "wow" separation. Purdy later hit Pearsall for what might've been a catch-and-run TD 🏈Excellent Renardo Green leaping PBU 🏈CMC has a lot of juice to begin this camp. Jordan James got most of the work behind him early in this practice, but the back half featured more of rookie Kaelon Black. He had a muscle-on-muscle collision with Marques Sigle early 🏈Ji'Ayir Brown notched an acrobatic diving INT off a shorter pass from Purdy, who bounced back immediately with a chunk gainer to Mike Evans. Even with Christian Kirk (calf strain) sideline, the 49ers' WR corps already looks worlds ahead of last season's 🏈Vet CB Eli Apple, entering Year 11, notched a pick 6 off Kurtis Rourke on a pass intended for Junior Bergen. Rourke rebounded with a nice seam shot to Jordan Watkins for a long gain, and then Rourke and Bergen bounced back with a long TD connection to end practice that fired up the onlooking first teamers 🏈Fred Warner looks like Fred Warner. Whenever he makes a nice stop near the media, Warner pretends to tweet with his thumbs to ensure his nice plays are noted 🏈Trent Williams, who just turned 38, is much more buoyant than I remember from previous camps. He's often throwing and catching the football in between reps and even jokingly running and cutting with the ball 🏈Another Kyle Shanahan cameo
summary:
49ers training camp practice #2 is in the books. Here are some of the highlights:

🏈De'Zhaun Stribling is getting OPEN — catch-and-run house call from Mac Jones with those long 4.36 strides... The rookie also created separation down the seam on a ball Purdy overshot. Stribling caught a nice one from Purdy on an early rollout
🏈New CB Jack Jones has looked spry, but Ricky Pearsall cooked him on a double move — Jones misfired but that was some "wow" separation. Purdy later hit Pearsall for what might've been a catch-and-run TD
🏈Excellent Renardo Green leaping PBU
🏈CMC has a lot of juice to begin this camp. Jordan James got most of the work behind him early in this practice, but the back half featured more of rookie Kaelon Black. He had a muscle-on-muscle collision with Marques Sigle early
🏈Ji'Ayir Brown notched an acrobatic diving INT off a shorter pass from Purdy, who bounced back immediately with a chunk gainer to Mike Evans. Even with Christian Kirk (calf strain) sideline, the 49ers' WR corps already looks worlds ahead of last season's
🏈Vet CB Eli Apple, entering Year 11, notched a pick 6 off Kurtis Rourke on a pass intended for Junior Bergen. Rourke rebounded with a nice seam shot to Jordan Watkins for a long gain, and then Rourke and Bergen bounced back with a long TD connection to end practice that fired up the onlooking first teamers
🏈Fred Warner looks like Fred Warner. Whenever he makes a nice stop near the media, Warner pretends to tweet with his thumbs to ensure his nice plays are noted
🏈Trent Williams, who just turned 38, is much more buoyant than I remember from previous camps. He's often throwing and catching the football in between reps and even jokingly running and cutting with the ball
🏈Another Kyle Shanahan cameo
